judgements.justification: Three of A's four reviewers said they could not judge the paper (6Pv4 and yA7o left the proofs unchecked; rBKj knew the key prior work only 'at a high level') and all rated 6; A's area chair took the flat 6s as the verdict. In B only iUkv said so.
Neither committee had an outlying reviewer. A's area chair followed four uniform 6s, and B's area chair went beyond all three reviewers.
The verbal assessments differ, not only the scores. A's h23K called the contribution 'not major', while B's kvzq called it 'a very strong contribution'.
A's unanimous 6s led to the lower tier, a poster. The higher tier went to B, whose scores were spread.
iUkv rose from 5 to 6 on notation answers that can be checked against the paper, not on copied results or new evidence.
B's meta-review carries the readability concern forward ('Please take remarks on readability serious'). A's meta-review names its main weakness, the difficulty of following the paper.
kvzq's rank-condition error and iUkv's sum-over-z error were questions and minor points. Neither was a stated ground for a score or for the recommendation.
The authors conceded open completeness and deferred experiments to both committees. The paper already stated these facts, and neither concession lifted a score.
yA7o's 2021-09-10 update raised no new objection and changed no score; it only restated earlier concerns.
The scores were not near-identical (A 6/6/6/6, B 8/6/7). B's area chair chose the oral on its own reading, not a different cut-off on the same reviews.
Neither area chair set aside a better-informed reviewer's verdict. A's most specific reviewer, h23K, also rated 6, and B's confidence-4 reviewer, kvzq, supported the paper.

B's main concern, notation, was answered in the response and moved iUkv from 5 to 6. A's main concerns (Theorem 2 depth, journal fit, the continuous case, missing experiments) could not be fixed in a response, and no A score moved.
No score stood apart in either committee; A rated 6/6/6/6 and B rated 8/6/7.
Neither committee had an outlying reviewer.
Neither committee had a detractor whom the area chair set aside.
A's 6Pv4 judged the paper better suited to a journal because its proofs need days to check, and stage 1 lists that among A's reasons for the poster. B raised no venue-fit point.
Neither meta-review misreports the record. B's correctly notes that one reviewer raised its score, and A's reports discussion without misstating positions.
Both committees left most of the response unanswered: B's 9UEy and kvzq never replied. A's yA7o did post an update, so the silence is not one-sided.
The reviewers who said they could not verify the paper gave borderline 6s, not clear accept scores. Their scores held means down instead of lifting them.
Neither committee was split between accept and reject; every score was 6 or higher.
Stage 1 finds the authors' accounts consistent. Both committees heard that completeness is open, and the rank-condition answer matches the paper.
No novelty verdict rested on a wrong account of prior work. h23K's MGT reduction is correct, and kvzq's error concerns this paper's assumptions, not prior work.
B's oral exceeds its scores (top 8, 'Top 50% of accepted'). No reviewer asked for it, and the meta-review gives only 'a solid and novel theoretical contribution' as grounds.
A's critics objected to depth, the missing experiments and readability, not to the paper's framing from another field's premises.
B's higher raters did not engage after the rebuttal. A's tied top rater, rBKj, read closely for 7 hours, so the light-review contrast that the reason requires is absent.
Neither committee rejected the paper, and neither judged the promised fixes too large.
Neither area chair used an off-record assessment to settle a split. 9UEy's sight of the ICML reviews was a reviewer's input, and nothing shows that it moved a score.
A's yA7o required experiments of an identification-theory paper and held their absence against it. B's kvzq said a theory paper should not be penalised for that.
No reviewer on either committee held a below-threshold score.
